title: Levy (2009): Multiple Choice
instructions: Choose the single best answer supported by the article.

items.prompt: Which is NOT one of the four components of stereotype embodiment theory?
options: Internalization across the life span
Genetic inevitability
Operation outside conscious awareness
Salience gained from self-relevance
items.explanation: The four components are internalization, unconscious operation, self-relevance, and multiple pathways. Genetic inevitability is not a component.

items.prompt: What motivates a psychosocial approach to aging in this article?
options: Substantial cultural variation in older adults' health
The absence of any biological changes during adulthood
Young adults' complete immunity to age stereotypes
The claim that medical institutions alone determine health
items.answer: Substantial cultural variation in older adults' health
items.explanation: An account based entirely on inevitable physiological decline does not adequately explain cultural differences in older adults' health.

items.prompt: Which interpretation of the Ohio longitudinal findings is most accurate?
options: Positive thinking guarantees an additional 7.5 years for every person
The negative-self-perception group lived 7.5 years longer on average
The study followed children for six months
The positive group retained functional and average survival advantages after adjustment
items.answer: The positive group retained functional and average survival advantages after adjustment
items.explanation: Participants were at least 50 at baseline and followed for more than two decades. The average 7.5-year difference was observational, not a guaranteed individual causal effect.

items.prompt: Why may younger adults internalize negative age stereotypes without defending against them?
options: They already identify themselves as older adults
Media expose them only to positive images of aging
They do not yet feel that the stereotypes target them
The law requires them to learn age stereotypes
items.answer: They do not yet feel that the stereotypes target them
items.explanation: When stereotypes do not feel self-directed, people may feel little need to resist them and later carry those beliefs into old age.

items.prompt: What did the Baltimore study find in its subgroup aged 18–39 at baseline?
options: The two stereotype groups had identical cardiovascular risks
The positive group had twice the event risk before age 38
The negative group was twice as likely to have an event after age 60
Television viewing entirely accounted for cardiovascular risk
items.answer: The negative group was twice as likely to have an event after age 60
items.explanation: In the subgroup of 229 participants, more negative baseline age stereotypes predicted twice the likelihood of a cardiovascular event after 60, after covariate adjustment.

items.prompt: Why did the priming studies use a presentation duration of 55 milliseconds?
options: To let participants consciously memorize every word
To permit encoding while preventing conscious perception
To diagnose eye disease during the experiment
To measure reaction speed without activating stereotypes
items.answer: To permit encoding while preventing conscious perception
items.explanation: This duration was used to test whether age stereotypes could influence outcomes without participants consciously perceiving the stimulus.

items.prompt: In the will-to-live experiment, what did positive-stereotype participants tend to choose?
options: A life-prolonging intervention despite its costs
An intervention only when no financial costs were mentioned
Immediate rejection of every intervention regardless of its costs
Delegation of the entire decision to younger people
items.answer: A life-prolonging intervention despite its costs
items.explanation: The scenarios included loss of savings and extensive family care. Positive priming favored acceptance, whereas negative priming favored rejection.

items.prompt: How are the objective and subjective onsets of old age related?
options: They always occur on exactly the same day
Subjective onset is unaffected by institutional cues
Objective onset is determined only by biological tests
Formal age thresholds are distinct from subjective onset but may contribute to it
items.answer: Formal age thresholds are distinct from subjective onset but may contribute to it
items.explanation: Arbitrary thresholds, such as senior admission prices or Social Security enrollment, may contribute to recognizing old age as one's present state.

items.prompt: Which is an institutional cue that can make age stereotypes self-relevant?
options: An older person freely choosing positive words
Friends sharing hobbies without age-based restrictions
A child solving a mathematics problem
An older person being denied employment or appropriate medical treatment
items.answer: An older person being denied employment or appropriate medical treatment
items.explanation: Levy distinguishes interpersonal cues, such as patronizing speech, from institutional cues in employment and medical care.

items.prompt: Which example best illustrates the stereotype-matching effect?
options: All stereotype content produces identical effects on every task
Physical stereotypes have stronger effects on a corresponding physical task
Researchers exclude all older participants to avoid an unwanted finding
Positive primes operate only when consciously perceived
items.answer: Physical stereotypes have stronger effects on a corresponding physical task
items.explanation: Corresponding stereotype content and outcome domains appear to strengthen expectations directed at the relevant outcome.

items.prompt: Which finding most directly supports the behavioral pathway?
options: Negative primes increased immediate cardiovascular stress responses
Younger adults showed weaker responses to the same priming protocol
Positive self-perceptions predicted healthier practices over the next 18 years
Television exposure was identical across cultures and age groups
items.answer: Positive self-perceptions predicted healthier practices over the next 18 years
items.explanation: Differences in practices such as taking prescribed medication illustrate how beliefs may influence health through behavior.

items.prompt: What direction of response is shown in Figure 2?
options: Positive priming reduced stress responses; negative priming increased them
Both kinds of priming completely eliminated stress responses
The priming conditions produced identical responses
Positive priming increased responses; negative priming reduced them
items.answer: Positive priming reduced stress responses; negative priming increased them
items.explanation: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure and skin conductance showed opposing response directions under positive and negative age-stereotype priming.

items.prompt: Which intervention challenge does Levy identify for future work?
options: Legally banning every age-related word with any negative connotation
Sustaining positive age-stereotype activation in everyday life
Discontinuing physiological research on older adults
Restricting future experiments to younger participants
items.answer: Sustaining positive age-stereotype activation in everyday life
items.explanation: Laboratory experiments demonstrated the potential of positive priming; maintaining that activation in daily life remains a challenge.

items.prompt: Which distinctive feature of age stereotypes does the article identify?
options: Younger people who stereotype older people will join that group if they live long enough
The people applying a stereotype and its targets remain permanently separate
Age stereotypes cannot contain positive beliefs or self-perceptions
Age stereotypes are learned exclusively at school
items.answer: Younger people who stereotype older people will join that group if they live long enough
items.explanation: Unlike membership in many other targeted groups, membership in the older age group is a prospective transition for younger people who survive long enough.

items.prompt: Which description best captures the article's research approach?
options: A single cross-sectional analysis of a new sample
A manual containing only clinical treatment guidelines
A theoretical synthesis of experimental and longitudinal evidence
A biological experiment unrelated to stereotypes
items.answer: A theoretical synthesis of experimental and longitudinal evidence
items.explanation: Levy organizes prior experimental and longitudinal findings into the four components of stereotype embodiment theory.
